entries.title: Proverbs 29:1
segments: Obstinate residence to reproof is an alarming indication of approaching ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:2
segments: Since the welfare of a state depends upon the character of its rulers, it is the duty of all who exercise the elective franchise to prefer the righteous above the wicked, and to elevate to office able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:4
segments:
Gifts; bribes to pervert judgment. 
 
No government or community can prosper in which the administration of justice is corrupted by bribery.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:6
segments:
A snare; to take his own feet. 
 
  Doth sing and rejoice; because his path is free from snares.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:8
segments:
Bring a city into a snare; or, set it on fire; fill it with strife and faction. 
 
  Turn away wrath; appease the angry passions of the people, and avert God's anger.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:9
segments:
No rest; to the wise man.  He will find it a bootless and uncomfortable contest. 
 
No controversy is more profitless than that which is carried on with one who cannot feel the force of sound arguments.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:10
segments: Seek his soul; love him, and protect his life and interests.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:13
segments: Deceitful man; or, "usurer;" who loans to the poor.
Since they both share God's common bounty, they are bound to regard and treat each other as brethren.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:15
segments: No child becomes wise and virtuous by pursuing his own inclinations, but only by faithful instruction and discipline.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:18
segments:
Vision; revelation of divine truth. 
 
  Perish; or as the Hebrew may be rendered, are made dissolute. 
 
  Keepeth the law; this implies that he lives where there is a "vision." 
 
The faithful dispensation of divine truth is the only hope of a nation. Where this is wanting the people will sink into ignorance and corruption, till their destruction becomes inevitable.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:19
segments:
Words; that is, mere words. 
 
  Though he understand; the commands and reproofs of his master. 
 
  He will not answer; in a dutiful spirit; that is, he will not render prompt obedience.  The proverb inculcates the necessity of timely chastisement.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:21
segments:
Delicately bringeth up; spoils by indulgence. 
 
  Become his son at the length; the servant will, in the issue, claim to be treated as a son.  But we may understand this proverb of the careful training of a servant of superior worth, so that in the end he takes the place of a son to his master.  Compare

entries.title: Proverbs 29:24
segments: Heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not; is privy to or conceals the false oaths of his companion, and thus shares with him the guilt of perjury.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:25
segments:
The fear of man bringeth a snare; leads us in many ways into sin. 
 
He who is swayed by the opinions of his fellow men, rather than by God's word, will be betrayed into innumerable sins and errors, which will prove a snare to his soul.  It is only by faith in God that we can overcome the fear of man, and pursue with steadfastness a course of integrity.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:26
segments: Every man's judgment cometh from the Lord; it is to him alone that we can confidently look for justice and deliverance.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:27
segments: The whole history of the world from the beginning, is but a fulfilment of the original declaration in Eden: "I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed.
